test_title: SSC Selection Post HSC Level Official Paper (Held on: 4 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The ‘Vikramshila University’ in Bihar was founded by which of the following kings?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Dharampala__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​​**

__
 
• **Dharampala**

 
 
• **Buddhism enjoyed the enormous support of Dharmapala.**
 
• He restored Nalanda University and gave it 200 villages.
 
• He established the Vikramashila monastery, which later developed into a** significant Buddhist study centre.**
 
• One of the finest kings of the** Pala dynasty, Dharmapala **(770–810 AD), also went by the names Paramabhattaraka, Paramesvara, and **Maharajadhiraja.**
 
• One of the biggest Buddhist universities was **Vikramashila**, which had over a hundred lecturers and over a thousand pupils.
 
• It produced great academics who were frequently invited by other nations to spread **Buddhist knowledge, culture, and religion.**
 
• During the** Pala Empire, the two most significant centers **of learning in India were Nalanda and Vikramshila.
 
• In the year 1193, an army under the command of **Sultan Bakhtiyar Khilji of Turkey **destroyed** **Vikramashila University.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__​**

 
• Gopala II

 
 
• **Gopala II, the sixth king of the Pala line to govern for at least four years**, succeeded the Pala monarch Shurapala I in the Bengal-Bihar region of the** Indian subcontinent.**
 
 
 
• Devapala
 
 
• The Pala Empire of Bengal, located in the Indian Subcontinent,** was ruled by Devapala,** who was its most powerful king.
 
• He succeeded his father** Dharamapala as the third king in the line.**
 
• In the Indian Subcontinent's **Bihar and Bengal provinces**, Gopala founded the Pala dynasty.
 
• His name Pala's final morpheme, which signifies** "protector," **was also adopted as the name's ending for all Pala kings.
